# Instructor guide {#sec-instructor}

::: {.content-hidden when-profile="instructor"}
This chapter is for teaching staff. Worked solutions, expected values and
timings appear only in the instructor build:

```bash
quarto render --profile instructor
```

which writes to `_book-instructor/`. Students are not missing anything they need.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-profile="instructor"}

## Before the day

- Render and skim `_book-instructor/` — the per-exercise answers live in the
  chapters themselves, not here, so that an answer is never far from the task it
  belongs to.
- Run `Rscript scripts/make_data.R` and commit the CSVs, so that every student
  has byte-identical files and the expected values below hold.
- Print the worksheets: `python3 scripts/make_worksheet.py --day 1 --profile
  student`, then `quarto render print/day1-student.qmd --to typst`. Fourteen
  pages, double-sided.
- Send @sec-setup out a week ahead and ask for a reply confirming
  `source("checks/checks.R"); hds_check()` printed all `[ok]`. Installing R,
  Python and six packages in the first ten minutes of a session does not work;
  chasing it by email the week before does.

## Shape of the day

The three exercises are 45, 60 and 60 minutes plus a 20-minute plenary, which
fits a three-hour session with one break. Two compressions work:

**90 minutes.** Exercise 1.2 Tasks 1–2 and Exercise 1.3 Tasks 1, 3 and 4. Drop
Exercise 1.1 entirely and set it as pre-work; drop every stretch task. The day
still lands if, and only if, the baseline comparison and the refitted
coefficients survive.

**Two 90-minute sessions.** Session one: 1.1 and 1.2 with stretches. Session
two: 1.3 with Stretch 1 (the decision tree), which is the strongest single
result in the day and is usually cut for time.

## Mixed cohorts

This cohort splits predictably into students who arrive fluent in R from
Modules 1–2 and students who arrive fluent in Python from a computing
background. Pair across the divide in 1.1 and 1.3, and let them work in their
own language in 1.2, where the task is the pipeline rather than the syntax.

The statistically strong students are the ones most likely to object that this
is "just regression with extra steps". That objection is correct about the
model and wrong about the question, and it is worth answering in plenary rather
than at a desk: Module 2 asked whether age is associated with length of stay,
this module asks whether a number produced for a patient who was not in the
dataset is close enough to act on. Same estimator, different claim, different
evidence required.

## Expected values, all in one place

Regenerated data varies in the last digit; quote ranges to students.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Original coefficients (intercept, Age, Severity) | −8.4, 0.93, 3.44 |
| Test MAE, linear model (R split) | ≈ 3.4 days |
| Test MAE, linear model (Python split) | ≈ 3.2 days |
| Baseline (predict-the-mean) MAE | ≈ 13.0 days |
| Test MAE across 20 seeds | 3.0 – 3.7 days |
| 5-fold CV MAE (mean, sd) | 3.41, 0.16 |
| MAE on extract A / B / C | ≈ 3.6 / 3.5 / 22.7 |
| Refitted Age coefficient, A / B / C | 0.95 / 0.95 / 0.13 |
| Decision tree MAE: test / A / B / C | 5.9 / 5.9 / 9.9 / 29.9 |
| Birth weight: test MAE / baseline MAE | ≈ 190–220 g / ≈ 310–340 g |

: {tbl-colwidths="[62,38]"}

The three rows that carry the day's teaching are the baseline comparison
(13.0 against 3.4), extract B (covariate shift, no loss of accuracy) and the
tree on extract B (covariate shift, accuracy halved).

## The one thing not to rush

Exercise 1.3 Task 3 — refitting on each extract and comparing coefficients.
Everything before it can be done by pattern-matching the worked example. Task 3
is the only point in the day where a student must decide what evidence would
answer a question, and the plenary depends on it. If the session is running
late, cut Task 2's plots and the stretches, never Task 3.

## Known rough edges

- The simulated LOS is implausible (median ≈ 66 days, symmetric). This is
  deliberate and is Task 1 of Exercise 1.2, but say so in plenary; otherwise a
  clinically trained student spends the morning quietly assuming the whole
  exercise is nonsense.
- `scripts/make_data.R` contains the Exercise 1.3 key. Exclude `scripts/` from
  the published site if that matters to you.
- The worked answers are hidden until you release them: set `show-solutions: true`
  in `_quarto.yml`, `make site`, and push. Doing that straight after the session
  gives students something to check against while the attempt is fresh.
- Students who complete Stretch 2 of Exercise 1.2 will report a different test
  MAE from the booklet's. That is the stretch task working.

:::
